description:
In this conversation, we sit down with Carl Pei, founder of Nothing, to talk about how he built a phone company from scratch in a hypercompetitive market like India. We get into how Nothing stood out not by having the biggest budget but by noticing a simple thing: all the big brands were trying to sell to everyone, which meant nobody was really selling to anyone specific.

We then go deep on how a phone actually gets made, from deciding what the product stands for to managing hundreds of supplier relationships, keeping cash from getting stuck in inventory, and shipping on time when delays cost millions. Carl also talks about where Nothing is headed with AI, what Essential Apps is really pointing toward, and why he thinks the entire idea of an operating system is going to change completely within the next few years.
